“In accordance with the Americans with Disabilities Act of 1990, if you require a
disability related modification or accommodation to attend or participate in this
meeting, including auxiliary aids or services, please call the City Clerk’s office at
310-952-1720 at least 48 hours prior to the meeting.” (Government Code Section
54954.2)
PUBLIC INFORMATION

The public may address the members of the City Council on any matters within the
jurisdiction of the City Council or on any items on the agenda of the City Council
during the designated public comment periods. There will be two Oral
Communication sessions: one for Agendized Items (comment about items ON the
agenda) and the other for non-Agendized items (comment about items NOT on the
Agenda). The Oral Communications portion of the agenda is limited to a duration of
one hour unless otherwise approved by the City Council. Comment time is normally
3 minutes depending on the number of speakers.

Because of the threat of COVID-19 (the “Coronavirus”) you are urged to take all
appropriate health safety precautions. Wearing masks is not required but is highly
recommended while inside Carson City Hall. Temperatures will be checked for those
experiencing any symptoms of COVID-19, prior to entering the City Hall.

PUBLIC VIEWING AVAILABLE BY:

- Livestream on the City’s website: The meeting will be streamed live over the
internet  via:  www.carsonca.gov  or on  Youtube:
www.youtube.com/c/CityofCarsonCaliforniaOfficialYouTubePage

- Cable TV: Spectrum (Channel 35) and ATT (Channel 99)

CITY OF CARSON  Page 1
 Housing Authority/Successor Agency/City Council  AGENDA  TUESDAY, NOVEMBER 7, 2023

IF YOU ARE NOT ABLE TO ATTEND THE MEETING IN-PERSON, PUBLIC COMMENTS
CAN BE SUBMITTED BEFORE THE MEETING AT/VIA:

- Email: Public comments can be emailed to cityclerk@carsonca.gov. The cut-off
time to submit any email communications is 3:00 p.m. on the day of the meeting.

- Written: Written comments can be dropped off at the City Clerk’s Office or in the
white box outside City Hall. The cut-off time to submit any written communications is
3:00 p.m. on the day of the meeting. Written comments dropped off at the City
Clerk’s Office or at the white box or any email received will not be read aloud at
Council Meeting but will be circulated to the City Council and incorporated into the
record.

PUBLIC INFORMATION

The public may address the members of the City Council on any matters within the jurisdiction of the City Council or on any items on the agenda of the City Council during the designated public comment periods. There will be two Oral Communication sessions: one for Agendized Items (comment about items ON the agenda) and the other for non-Agendized items (comment about items NOT on the Agenda). The Oral Communications portion of the agenda is limited to a duration of one hour unless otherwise approved by the City Council. Comment time is normally 3 minutes depending on the number of speakers.

Because of the threat of COVID-19 (the “Coronavirus”) you are urged to take all appropriate health safety precautions. Wearing masks is not required but is highly recommended while inside Carson City Hall. CONSENT (Items 16 to 33) Presented by City Manager Roberts
Discussion led by Public Works Director Arlington Rodgers- "Streets Project" 

MPT expressed concern about in district one and forgetting Galaxy West and Centerview and requested weekly updates on the project. 
Director Rodgers stated that at the next council meeting there will be a request for project managers and inspectors to oversee the project. 
MPT Hilton reiterated that Carson use to have beautiful streets and looks forward to the city returning to how it use to be and that the entire city looks good from one end of the city to the next regardless of.

Mayor Davis-Holmes asked why only $2 million dollars per district. City Manager Roberts explained that because we are so far into the fiscal year and the rainy season is coming, that was the allocation made. David explained there will be an inconvenience for the residents because the work is happening simultaneously. PIO will share routes online for residents to know. David also explained the money is coming from the reserved, so the budget won't be structurally balanced. Mayor said if you get to a point where you need more than 2 million, please ask. Because that is what the UUT and the sales tax was for. The residents do not want to hear about a surplus, they want their streets fixed. 

Councilman Hicks asked about the current CIP. Is this in addition to or replacing CIP program? Director Rodgers shared that this streets project is in addition to the CIP. He also said residents should not be alarmed if one street gets fixed and another nearby doesn't. Public Works is using an index so not all streets will be done at the same time. Using the PCI, streets will be fixed based on that index. Gray color versus black color does not indicate what order the streets need to be done. 
Councilman Dear asked about a number of streets that have cracks but no potholes. Director Rodgers said that streets with cracks will get paved as all streets are being paved eventually. But some streets will need to be assessed to fit into a systematic approach. 

Councilwoman Rojas thanked Arlington on the great work he has been able to accomplish in eight months. Director Rodgers acknowledged his team and the city manager's office. 

Mayor Davis-Holmes asked about the medians and the trees. Director Rodgers talked about heading into the rainy season and begin planning for what we want the medians to look like in the spring and summer. Mulch is being placed in certain areas to avoid weeds. Regarding the trees, West Coast Arborist remains the city's contracts. All trees don't have to be trimmed as often as other trees. Some require more and some require less depending on the species of the trees. Tee trimming schedule will be on the city's website. Mayor Davis-Holmes asked if the council aids can be informed of the tree trimming schedule. 
Mayor Davis-Holmes asked about graffiti. Director Rodgers stated that the recent approval is allowing for future graffiti abatement. 
MPT Hilton made the motion
Second by Mayor Davis-Holmes
Councilman Dear mentioned the 3 year project that took place on Figueroa and wants to make sure the Sanitation District pays for that. 
Councilman Hicks mentioned some street lights that are out especially with the time change 
Director Rodgers shared that a citywide sidewalk plan is coming soon for council's approval. 
The vote is unanimous, motion carries.
